title: Static Website Acceleration with S3 & CloudFront OAC
goal: Goal: Securely serve static S3 assets globally through CloudFront while restricting direct public access to S3 using Origin Access Control (OAC).

concepts.title: Origin Access Control (OAC)
concepts.body: The modern AWS recommended feature to secure S3 origins by restricting access strictly to authorized CloudFront distributions.

concepts.title: OAC vs Legacy OAI
concepts.body: OAC supports all S3 buckets in all Regions, SSE-KMS encryption, dynamic HTTP requests, and improved security posture compared to legacy Origin Access Identity (OAI).

concepts.title: S3 Bucket Policy Restriction
concepts.body: S3 bucket policy conditions allow s3:GetObject only when aws:SourceArn matches the CloudFront distribution ARN.

concepts.title: Global Edge Caching
concepts.body: CloudFront caches static content at edge locations worldwide, reducing latency and backend S3 read requests.

concepts.title: OAC vs Legacy OAI Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureOrigin Access Control (OAC)Origin Access Identity (OAI)StatusAWS Recommended (Current Standard)Legacy (Maintenance Mode)点SSE-KMS EncryptionSupported nativelyNot supportedAll S3 RegionsSupported globally across all AWS RegionsLimited in newer AWS RegionsHTTP MethodsSupports GET, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETESupports GET / HEAD onlyPolicy conditionaws:SourceArn matching distribution ARNaws:PrincipalARN matching OAI ID

whyItMatters: This matters because OAC (the modern replacement for legacy OAI) and restricting S3 public access are constantly tested on SAA-C03.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity CloudFront permissions: cloudfront:CreateDistribution, cloudfront:CreateOriginAccessControl, cloudfront:GetDistribution S3 permissions: s3:CreateBucket, s3:PutBucketPolicy, s3:PutObject Cleanup: cloudfront:DeleteDistribution, s3:DeleteBucket
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Create a Private S3 Bucket and Upload Static Files

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 Console.
Choose Region us-east-1.
Click Create bucket.
Set Bucket name to saa-oac-private-site-[account-id].
Keep Block all public access enabled.
Click Create bucket.
Upload an index.html file into the private bucket.

consoleSteps.note: Keeping Block Public Access enabled ensures the bucket cannot be accessed directly from the public internet.

consoleSteps.title: Create CloudFront Distribution with Origin Access Control (OAC)

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudFront Console.
Click Create distribution.
Under Origin domain, select your private bucket saa-oac-private-site-[account-id].s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com.
Under Origin access, select Origin access control settings (recommended).
Click Create control setting.
Set Name to saa-s3-oac-control and Signing behavior to Sign requests (recommended).
Click Create.
Under Viewer protocol policy, select Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Set Default root object to index.html.
Click Create distribution.

consoleSteps.note: OAC signs requests sent from CloudFront to S3 using AWS signature version 4.

consoleSteps.title: Attach OAC S3 Bucket Policy

instructions.text: On the distribution details page, copy the autogenerated S3 bucket policy.
Open Amazon S3 Console -> Select saa-oac-private-site-[account-id].
Choose Permissions tab -> Click Edit bucket policy.
Paste the policy granting s3:GetObject permission strictly to cloudfront.amazonaws.com with condition matching your distribution ARN.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.note: Bucket policy condition ensures only your specific CloudFront distribution can fetch objects.

consoleSteps.title: Test Distribution URL and Verify Restricted S3 Access

instructions.text: Copy the Distribution domain name (e.g. d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net).
Open the CloudFront domain URL in your browser to verify the website loads via HTTPS.
Open the raw S3 object URL directly in your browser to confirm direct S3 access returns 403 Access Denied.

consoleSteps.note: Confirms content is served globally via CloudFront while S3 remains completely private.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Select your CloudFront distribution -> Click Disable.
Wait for status to show Disabled -> Click Delete.
Empty and delete S3 bucket saa-oac-private-site-[account-id].

consoleSteps.warning: CloudFront distributions must be disabled before they can be deleted.

cleanup.text: Remove any function or Lambda@Edge associations from the CloudFront distribution.
Disable the CloudFront distribution and wait until the status changes to Disabled.
Delete the CloudFront distribution, Origin Access Control, and test S3 bucket.

cheatSheet.title: Origin Access Control (OAC)
cheatSheet.body: AWS recommended method for securing S3 origins behind CloudFront. Replaces legacy OAI.

cheatSheet.title: S3 Bucket Policy Condition
cheatSheet.body: Uses `StringEquals` on `AWS:SourceArn` matching `arn:aws:cloudfront::123456789012:distribution/DIST_ID`.

cheatSheet.title: Viewer Protocol Policy
cheatSheet.body: Choose **Redirect HTTP to HTTPS** to enforce encrypted communication between clients and edge locations.

troubleshooting.title: 403 Forbidden on CloudFront URL
troubleshooting.body: Verify that the S3 Bucket Policy grants `s3:GetObject` to `cloudfront.amazonaws.com` and that `aws:SourceArn` matches the CloudFront distribution ARN.

examTraps.title: Legacy OAI vs OAC Traps
examTraps.body: Always choose Origin Access Control (OAC) for modern S3 bucket origin security. OAI is legacy and does not support SSE-KMS.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master Amazon CloudFront concepts and global edge distribution patterns in Amazon CloudFront.

title: Multi-Origin Routing & Path-Based Behaviors (ALB + S3)
goal: Goal: Route dynamic requests to an Application Load Balancer and static media to S3 under a single domain.

concepts.title: Multi-Origin Distribution
concepts.body: A single CloudFront distribution can connect to multiple backend origins (e.g. ALBs, EC2 instances, S3 buckets, or custom HTTP endpoints).

concepts.title: Path Pattern Behaviors
concepts.body: Cache behaviors evaluate URL paths in order (e.g., /images/*, /api/*, Default (*)) to route requests to specific origins with tailored TTL and caching policies.

concepts.title: Hybrid Caching Policies
concepts.body: Dynamic ALB paths can disable caching (TTL=0) or forward query strings/headers, while static S3 image paths use aggressive edge caching (CachingOptimized).

concepts.title: Single Domain Simplification
concepts.body: Consolidates static assets and dynamic APIs under one custom domain (e.g. example.com), avoiding Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) complexity.

concepts.title: Multi-Origin Path Routing Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: Path PatternTarget OriginCache PolicyForward Headers / Query Strings/images/*Amazon S3 BucketCachingOptimized (Aggressive Caching)None (Maximizes Cache Hit Ratio)/api/*Application Load BalancerCachingDisabledAll headers & query strings forwardedDefault (*)Application Load BalancerCustom / Managed PolicyForwarded based on application needs

whyItMatters: This matters because path-based origin routing, reducing domain complexity, and hybrid static/dynamic caching policies are heavily tested on SAA-C03.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

Open Amazon S3 Console -> Provision an S3 bucket saa-media-origin-[account-id] for static assets.

consoleSteps.title: Configure Multi-Origin CloudFront Distribution

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudFront Console -> Click Create distribution.

Under Viewer protocol policy, select Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

Set Path pattern to /images/*.
Set Target origin to saa-media-origin-[account-id].
Set Cache policy to CachingOptimized.
Click Create behavior.

consoleSteps.note: Directs all /images/* traffic to S3 with edge caching while default traffic routes to ALB.

consoleSteps.title: Verify Path Routing and Headers

instructions.text: Open CloudFront URL https:/// to verify dynamic ALB response.
Open CloudFront URL https:///images/logo.png to verify static S3 image response.

consoleSteps.note: Confirms path routing to distinct origins under a single domain.

cheatSheet.title: Multi-Origin Distributions
cheatSheet.body: Single distribution serving multiple origins (ALBs, S3, EC2) using path behaviors.

cheatSheet.title: Path Pattern Order
cheatSheet.body: CloudFront evaluates cache behaviors in precedence order from top to bottom before falling back to `Default (*)`.

cheatSheet.title: Single Domain Consolidation
cheatSheet.body: Eliminates CORS complexity by serving APIs (`/api/*`) and static media (`/images/*`) on one domain.

troubleshooting.title: Path Matching Failure
troubleshooting.body: Verify that path patterns use correct wildcard syntax (e.g. `/images/*`) and that precedence order lists specific paths above `Default (*)`.

examTraps.title: Multiple Distributions vs Multi-Origin Trap
examTraps.body: Do NOT create separate CloudFront distributions for static and dynamic paths of the same website. Use a single CloudFront distribution with multiple origins and path behaviors.

title: Restricting Content Access with CloudFront Signed URLs & Signed Cookies
goal: Goal: Protect premium or paid media content from unauthorized distribution using Trusted Key Groups, Signed URLs, and Signed Cookies.

concepts.title: Signed URLs vs Signed Cookies
concepts.body: Signed URLs: Restrict access to individual files (e.g. single video download). Signed Cookies: Restrict access to multiple files or an entire directory (e.g. subscriber-only streaming media).

concepts.title: Trusted Key Groups (Recommended)
concepts.body: Modern mechanism where public keys are uploaded to CloudFront key groups and referenced by cache behaviors to validate signatures.

concepts.title: Legacy CloudFront Key Pairs
concepts.body: Legacy mechanism requiring root account access to generate CloudFront key pairs. AWS strongly recommends Trusted Key Groups.

concepts.title: Signature Expiration & IP Restriction
concepts.body: Signed URL parameters include expiration timestamps (`DateLessThan`) and optional IP address restriction policies.

concepts.title: Signed URLs vs Signed Cookies vs S3 Presigned URLs Decision Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureCloudFront Signed URLsCloudFront Signed CookiesS3 Presigned URLsScopeSingle file / object access via CloudFrontMultiple files / directory access via CloudFrontSingle file access directly from S3Client compatibilityUniversal (HTML links)Requires browser cookie supportUniversal (Direct S3 REST endpoint)Use casePaid digital download, individual file streamPremium subscriber portal, HLS media streamsTemporary direct S3 object access or uploadCDN CachingCached at CloudFront edge locationsCached at CloudFront edge locationsDirect S3 read (Bypasses CDN edge)

whyItMatters: This matters because distinguishing between CloudFront Signed URLs (single file) vs Signed Cookies (directory/multiple files) vs S3 Presigned URLs is a primary exam topic on SAA-C03.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

consoleSteps.title: Generate Public/Private Key Pair for CloudFront Key Group

instructions.text: Generate an RSA 2048-bit key pair on your local computer: openssl genrsa -out private_key.pem 2048.
Extract public key: openssl rsa -pubout -in private_key.pem -out public_key.pem.

consoleSteps.note: RSA 2048-bit key pairs are required for signing CloudFront URLs and cookies.

consoleSteps.title: Create Public Key and Trusted Key Group in CloudFront

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudFront Console -> Click Public keys in left navigation -> Choose Create public key.
Set Name to saa-premium-public-key and paste public_key.pem file content.
Click Create public key and copy generated Key ID.
Click Key groups -> Choose Create key group.
Set Name to saa-premium-key-group and attach saa-premium-public-key.
Click Create key group.

consoleSteps.note: Trusted Key Groups allow delegating URL signing without AWS root account access.

consoleSteps.title: Restrict Behavior to Trusted Key Group

instructions.text: Open your CloudFront distribution -> Choose Behaviors tab -> Select /premium/* path.
Under Restrict viewer access, select Yes (Use signed URLs or signed cookies).
Select Trusted key groups (recommended) -> Attach saa-premium-key-group.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.note: Blocks all unauthorized requests that lack a valid cryptographic signature.

consoleSteps.title: Generate Signed URL and Test Restricted Access

instructions.text: Attempt to open https:///premium/video.mp4 directly in your browser (observe 403 Forbidden).
Use AWS CLI or SDK script with private_key.pem to generate a Signed URL with expiration timestamp DateLessThan.
Open the generated Signed URL to verify successful video playback.

consoleSteps.note: Validates that signed URLs grant temporary access while blocking unsigned attempts.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Remove key group restriction from distribution behavior.
Delete key group saa-premium-key-group.
Delete public key saa-premium-public-key.

consoleSteps.warning: Key groups cannot be deleted while attached to active behaviors.

cheatSheet.body: Use for individual file downloads or single streams when clients don't support cookies.

cheatSheet.title: Signed Cookies

cheatSheet.title: Trusted Key Groups

troubleshooting.title: 403 Missing Key Pair ID

title: Edge Perimeter Protection with AWS WAF & CloudFront
goal: Goal: Block malicious web traffic, SQL injections, and geo-restricted requests at the AWS edge before touching backend servers using AWS WAF and CloudFront.

concepts.title: AWS WAF Global Scope (us-east-1)
concepts.body: Web ACLs protecting CloudFront distributions MUST be created in the Global (CloudFront) scope, which resides physically in `us-east-1`.

concepts.title: AWS Managed Rule Groups
concepts.body: Pre-configured security rules maintained by AWS Threat Research to protect against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XSS, bots).

concepts.title: Rate-Based Rules
concepts.body: Automatically track request rates per client IP address over 5-minute sliding windows to mitigate Layer 7 HTTP flood DDoS attacks.

concepts.title: Edge Defense vs Origin Defense
concepts.body: Inspecting and blocking malicious requests at CloudFront edge locations prevents malicious traffic from reaching backend ALBs or EC2 instances.

concepts.title: AWS WAF Scope & Target Matrix
concepts.body: Web ACL ScopeMandatory RegionAttachable Target ResourcesCLOUDFRONT (Global)us-east-1 (N. Virginia)Amazon CloudFront DistributionsREGIONALAny specific AWS Region (e.g., eu-west-1)Application Load Balancers (ALB), Amazon API Gateway, AWS AppSync

whyItMatters: This matters because WAF + CloudFront integration for DDoS/OWASP Top 10 mitigation at the edge is a high-frequency SAA-C03 scenario.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

title: Dynamic Request Manipulation with CloudFront Functions vs Lambda@Edge
goal: Goal: Inspect and rewrite HTTP headers or redirect URLs closer to the user using CloudFront Functions and compare with Lambda@Edge.

concepts.title: CloudFront Functions
concepts.body: Lightweight JavaScript runtime executing at 225+ CloudFront Edge Locations. Ideal for high-scale, sub-millisecond tasks like URL rewrites, header manipulation, and token validation.

concepts.title: Lambda@Edge
concepts.body: Full Node.js or Python Lambda runtime executing at Regional Edge Caches. Supports network access, body manipulation, third-party API calls, and longer execution times.

concepts.title: Execution Events
concepts.body: Viewer Request / Response: Runs before cache lookup / before returning to viewer (Supports CloudFront Functions & Lambda@Edge). Origin Request / Response: Runs before cache miss goes to origin / after receiving origin response (Lambda@Edge only).

concepts.title: CloudFront Functions vs Lambda@Edge Decision Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureCloudFront FunctionsLambda@EdgeRuntimeJavaScript (ECMAScript v5.1)Node.js & PythonExecution location225+ Edge Locations (Viewer side)13+ Regional Edge Caches (Viewer & Origin side)Execution time5 seconds (Viewer) / 30 seconds (Origin)Max Memory2 MB128 MB to 10 GBNetwork / File AccessNo network or file system accessFull network & file system accessHTTP Body AccessNo body accessCan inspect & modify bodyPrimary Use CasesHeader rewrites, URL redirects, JWT validationDynamic SSR, image resizing, origin side auth

whyItMatters: This matters because choosing CloudFront Functions (lightweight, sub-ms, JavaScript, Viewer side) vs Lambda@Edge (full Node.js/Python, network calls, Origin side) is a classic SAA-C03 question.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

cheatSheet.title: CloudFront Functions
cheatSheet.body: Lightweight JavaScript at 225+ edge locations. Sub-ms latency, high scale, no network access. Ideal for header rewrites & URL redirects.

cheatSheet.title: Lambda@Edge
cheatSheet.body: Node.js/Python at 13+ Regional Edge Caches. Full network/file access, up to 10 GB memory. Ideal for image processing & third-party API calls.

cheatSheet.title: Origin Request/Response
cheatSheet.body: Origin events can ONLY trigger Lambda@Edge; CloudFront Functions only support Viewer events.

title: High Availability & Origin Failover Groups
goal: Goal: Ensure zero downtime for static/dynamic origins if a primary origin fails by configuring automatic CloudFront Origin Failover Groups.

concepts.title: Origin Groups & Automated Failover
concepts.body: Combines two origins (Primary and Secondary) into a logical failover group. If the primary returns specific HTTP error codes, CloudFront automatically retries against the secondary.

concepts.title: Failover Criteria Status Codes
concepts.body: Configurable HTTP status codes triggering failover: 500, 502, 503, 504, 403, 404.

concepts.title: Cross-Region Failover Architecture
concepts.body: Primary origin in us-east-1 (e.g. S3 bucket or ALB) backed up by a secondary origin in eu-west-1 for high availability disaster recovery.

concepts.title: Seamless Client Recovery
concepts.body: CloudFront handles origin failover entirely at the CDN layer; end users never see 500-series origin errors.

concepts.title: Origin Failover Group Configuration Matrix
concepts.body: Origin RoleTarget ServiceAWS RegionFailover BehaviorPrimary OriginPrimary S3 Bucket / ALBus-east-1Handles 100% of normal trafficSecondary OriginSecondary S3 Bucket / ALBeu-west-1Receives traffic automatically if Primary returns 5xx/4xx error

whyItMatters: This matters because ensuring high availability and automated failover at the CDN layer is heavily tested on SAA-C03.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.

Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity CloudFront permissions: cloudfront:UpdateDistribution S3 permissions: s3:CreateBucket, s3:PutObject Cleanup: cloudfront:DeleteDistribution, s3:DeleteBucket

consoleSteps.title: Prepare Primary and Secondary Failover Origins

instructions.text: Create Primary S3 bucket saa-primary-origin-[account-id] in us-east-1.
Create Secondary S3 bucket saa-backup-origin-[account-id] in eu-west-1.
Upload test file index.html to both origins (primary containing text Primary Origin Active, secondary containing Backup Origin Active).

consoleSteps.note: Establishes multi-region backend origins for failover testing.

consoleSteps.title: Configure CloudFront Distribution with Two Origins

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudFront Console -> Open your distribution -> Choose Origins tab.
Ensure Origin 1 (Primary S3) and Origin 2 (Secondary S3) are both registered.

consoleSteps.note: Registers both origins in the distribution configuration.

consoleSteps.title: Create Origin Failover Group

instructions.text: In Origins tab, click Create origin group.
Set Name to saa-ha-origin-group.
Select Primary origin saa-primary-origin-[account-id].
Select Secondary origin saa-backup-origin-[account-id].
Under Failover criteria, check status codes 500, 502, 503, 504, 403, 404.
Click Create origin group.

consoleSteps.note: Creates the automated failover group.

consoleSteps.title: Attach Origin Group to Default Cache Behavior

instructions.text: Choose Behaviors tab -> Select Default (*) -> Click Edit.
Change Target origin to saa-ha-origin-group.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.note: Routes viewer requests to the origin group.

consoleSteps.title: Simulate Primary Origin Failure and Test Automatic Failover

instructions.text: Delete index.html from primary bucket (or block primary origin) to simulate failure.
Refresh CloudFront URL -> Confirm CloudFront automatically routes request to secondary backup origin (displaying Backup Origin Active).

consoleSteps.note: Validates seamless CDN-layer automated failover.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Remove origin group from behavior.
Delete origin group, distribution, and test S3 buckets.

consoleSteps.warning: Clean up test resources after testing.

cliSteps.note: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.

verification.text: Amazon CloudFront configuration verified in Amazon CloudFront.

cleanup.text: Remove any function or Lambda@Edge associations from the CloudFront distribution.
Disable the CloudFront distribution and wait until the status changes to Disabled.
Delete the CloudFront distribution, Origin Access Control, and test S3 bucket.

cheatSheet.title: Origin Failover Groups
cheatSheet.body: Provides high availability by automatically retrying requests against a secondary origin when the primary returns 5xx/4xx errors.

cheatSheet.title: Supported Failover Triggers
cheatSheet.body: Triggers on 500, 502, 503, 504, 403, and 404 HTTP status codes.

cheatSheet.title: Cross-Region Origins
cheatSheet.body: Primary and secondary origins can reside in different AWS Regions or different services (e.g. S3 + ALB).

troubleshooting.title: Failover Not Triggering
troubleshooting.body: Ensure the specific HTTP status code returned by the primary origin is selected in the Origin Group failover criteria.

examTraps.title: DNS Failover vs Origin Failover Trap
examTraps.body: Route 53 DNS failover takes minutes for DNS TTL cache propagation. For sub-second instant HTTP origin failover behind a CDN, choose CloudFront Origin Groups.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master Amazon CloudFront concepts and global edge distribution patterns in Amazon CloudFront.

memoryHook: Origin Group = Primary + Secondary | 5xx/4xx Error = Automatic Edge Failover

title: Custom SSL/TLS Certificates with ACM & SNI
goal: Goal: Attach a custom SSL/TLS domain certificate to a global distribution using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) and SNI.

concepts.title: ACM Certificate Region Requirement (us-east-1)
concepts.body: Public SSL/TLS certificates used with CloudFront distributions MUST be requested in the `us-east-1` (N. Virginia) Region regardless of where your origins reside.

concepts.title: Server Name Indication (SNI)
concepts.body: SNI allows multiple custom SSL certificates to be served from shared IP addresses at CloudFront edge locations without extra cost.

concepts.title: Alternate Domain Names (CNAMEs)
concepts.body: Allows routing your custom domain (e.g. app.example.com) to CloudFront (d1111.cloudfront.net).

concepts.title: DNS Validation & Managed Renewal
concepts.body: ACM validates domain ownership via DNS CNAME records and automatically renews public certificates before expiration without application downtime.

concepts.title: ACM Certificate Scope & Region Matrix
concepts.body: Target ResourceMandatory ACM Certificate RegionValidation OptionsCostAmazon CloudFront Distributionus-east-1 (N. Virginia) ONLYDNS Validation / Email ValidationFree ($0 for public ACM certs)Application Load Balancer (ALB)Same Region as the ALB (e.g., eu-west-1)DNS Validation / Email ValidationFree ($0 for public ACM certs)API Gateway Custom DomainSame Region as the API GatewayDNS Validation / Email ValidationFree ($0 for public ACM certs)

whyItMatters: This matters because ACM certificate region requirements (us-east-1 for edge distributions) and SNI support are heavily tested on SAA-C03.
costWarning: CloudFront requests, data transfer, invalidations, logging, Origin Shield and connected-service charges may apply. Complete cleanup promptly.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity ACM permissions: acm:RequestCertificate, acm:DescribeCertificate CloudFront permissions: cloudfront:UpdateDistribution Cleanup: acm:DeleteCertificate
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Request Public ACM Certificate in us-east-1

instructions.text: Open AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Console.
Ensure Region dropdown is set to us-east-1 (N. Virginia) (mandatory for CloudFront).
Click Request certificate -> Select Request a public certificate.
Enter Domain name (e.g. app.example.com or *.example.com).
Select Validation method DNS validation -> Click Request.

consoleSteps.note: CloudFront distributions can ONLY read ACM certificates created in us-east-1.

consoleSteps.title: Validate Certificate via Route 53 / DNS CNAME Records

instructions.text: Open certificate details page in ACM.
Click Create records in Route 53 (or copy generated CNAME name/value into your DNS provider).
Wait for Certificate status to transition to Issued.

consoleSteps.note: DNS validation allows ACM to manage automated annual certificate renewals.

consoleSteps.title: Attach Alternate Domain Name (CNAME) and Custom SSL Certificate

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudFront Console -> Select your distribution -> Click Edit.
Under Alternate domain name (CNAME), click Add item -> Enter app.example.com.
Under Custom SSL certificate, select the issued ACM certificate from us-east-1.
Under Support HTTP versions, keep SNI (Server Name Indication) selected (Free).
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.note: SNI allows custom SSL certificates on shared IP addresses at zero extra charge.

consoleSteps.title: Verify HTTPS Custom Domain SSL Handshake

instructions.text: Open terminal and test SSL handshake: curl -vI https://app.example.com.
Verify that the TLS certificate issuer displays Amazon and SNI domain matches.

consoleSteps.note: Validates secure TLS encryption over custom domain name.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Remove CNAME and custom certificate from CloudFront distribution.
Delete ACM certificate in us-east-1.

consoleSteps.warning: Unattach ACM certificates from CloudFront distributions before attempting deletion.

cliSteps.title: Check your AWS identity
cliSteps.note: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.

cliSteps.title: Request Certificate in us-east-1

commands.text: aws acm request-certificate --domain-name app.example.com --validation-method DNS --region us-east-1

cliSteps.note: Requests public ACM certificate in us-east-1.

verification.text: Amazon CloudFront configuration verified in Amazon CloudFront.

cleanup.text: Remove any function or Lambda@Edge associations from the CloudFront distribution.
Disable the CloudFront distribution and wait until the status changes to Disabled.
Delete the CloudFront distribution, Origin Access Control, and test S3 bucket.

cheatSheet.title: Mandatory ACM Region
cheatSheet.body: ACM certificates for CloudFront distributions MUST be created in **us-east-1 (N. Virginia)**.

cheatSheet.title: SNI (Server Name Indication)
cheatSheet.body: Allows serving custom SSL certificates on shared IP addresses at no extra charge. Legacy dedicated IP SSL costs $600/month.

cheatSheet.title: DNS Validation
cheatSheet.body: Recommended ACM validation method enabling automatic managed annual certificate renewals.

troubleshooting.title: ACM Certificate Not Listed in CloudFront
troubleshooting.body: Ensure the ACM certificate was requested in **us-east-1**. Certificates created in other regions (e.g. `eu-west-1`) will not appear in CloudFront.

examTraps.title: ACM Region Traps
examTraps.body: If an exam question asks where to create an ACM certificate for a CloudFront distribution, do NOT select the application origin region (e.g. `eu-west-1`). Select us-east-1.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master Amazon CloudFront concepts and global edge distribution patterns in Amazon CloudFront.

title: Non-HTTP Global Acceleration with AWS Global Accelerator
goal: Goal: Optimize global TCP/UDP traffic performance using AWS's private global fiber network and two static Anycast IP addresses.

concepts.title: AWS Global Accelerator Overview
concepts.body: Networking service that improves global application performance by routing user traffic over AWS's private global fiber network using two static Anycast IP addresses.

concepts.title: Static Anycast IP Addresses
concepts.body: Global Accelerator provides 2 fixed Anycast IP addresses announced from all AWS edge locations globally. Clients connect to the nearest edge location automatically.

concepts.title: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator
concepts.body: CloudFront: Caches HTTP/HTTPS web content at edge locations. Global Accelerator: Routes non-HTTP (TCP/UDP) or un-cacheable traffic over AWS private network without edge caching.

concepts.title: Sub-Second Automatic Health Check Failover
concepts.body: Global Accelerator monitors endpoint health continuously. If an ALB fails in one Region, traffic is rerouted to a healthy endpoint in another Region in seconds.

concepts.title: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureAmazon CloudFrontAWS Global AcceleratorSupported ProtocolsHTTP, HTTPS, WebSocketTCP, UDP, HTTP, HTTPSCaching LayerYes (Caches web content at 225+ edge locations)No Caching (Pass-through network acceleration)IP Address ModelDynamic CloudFront domain names2 Static Anycast IP AddressesPrimary Use CasesStatic websites, video streaming, REST APIsGaming (UDP), VoIP, IoT, multi-region failover, static IP whitelistNetwork PathPublic internet to Edge -> Edge to OriginPublic internet to Edge -> AWS Private Network to Endpoint

whyItMatters: This matters because distinguishing between CloudFront (HTTP caching at edge) vs Global Accelerator (TCP/UDP non-caching global Anycast routing) is a top SAA-C03 exam scenario.
costWarning: Low cost: AWS Global Accelerator costs $0.025/hr (~$0.60/day) plus small data transfer fees. Delete the accelerator immediately after completing your practice lab.

cheatSheet.title: AWS Global Accelerator
cheatSheet.body: Provides 2 static Anycast IPs and routes TCP/UDP traffic over AWS's private global network. No content caching.

cheatSheet.title: Static Anycast IPs
cheatSheet.body: IP addresses announced globally from edge locations. Eliminates DNS caching delay during failover.

cheatSheet.title: TCP / UDP Protocol Support
cheatSheet.body: Supports non-HTTP protocols like gaming (UDP), VoIP, IoT, and custom TCP applications.

troubleshooting.title: Endpoint Unhealthy in Accelerator
troubleshooting.body: Ensure the target ALB health check returns HTTP 200 OK and that security groups allow inbound traffic from Global Accelerator IP ranges.

examTraps.title: Non-HTTP & Static IP Traps
examTraps.body: If an exam question asks for UDP/TCP acceleration, static IP whitelisting, or fast multi-region failover without caching, do NOT select CloudFront. Select AWS Global Accelerator.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS Global Accelerator concepts and global edge distribution patterns in AWS Global Accelerator.
